clauses.verbatim_text: 1.1. This policy governs reimbursement of expenses genuinely and reasonably incurred by an employee in the course of Konkan Digital business — client work, internal meetings, training, and approved travel. It does not create an entitlement to spend up to any stated cap; caps are ceilings, not targets.
1.2. **Business purpose required.** Every claim must state a genuine business purpose. An expense with no identifiable business purpose is not reimbursable, regardless of amount or approval level.

conditions.text: expense must have a genuine business purpose

clauses.verbatim_text: 1.3. **Spend as if it were your own money.** Employees are expected to exercise the same judgment and care they would apply to their own funds — choosing reasonable, not lavish, options.

1.4. **Lowest reasonable cost.** Where multiple reasonable options exist (fare class, hotel category, vendor), the employee should choose the lowest-cost option that reasonably meets the business need, not the maximum the policy permits.
1.5. **No personal expenses.** Expenses for personal benefit, convenience unrelated to business need, or for family/dependents are not reimbursable under any clause of this policy (see also §19).

conditions.text: expense is for personal benefit, convenience unrelated to business need, or for family/dependents

clauses.verbatim_text: 1.6. Nothing in this policy overrides statutory tax withholding or reporting obligations; Finance may adjust the taxability of a reimbursement independently of whether it is approved for payment.

3.1. All air travel should be booked through the Travel Desk wherever possible; the Travel Desk has negotiated corporate fares and handles GST invoicing correctly. Self-booking is permitted when the Travel Desk cannot meet the required schedule, with intimation to the Reporting Manager.

conditions.text: Expense must be booked through the Travel Desk, or if self‑booked an intimation to the Reporting Manager must be provided

clauses.verbatim_text: 3.2. **Advance booking.** Domestic tickets should be booked at least 7 days in advance; international tickets at least 14 days in advance. Late booking without a documented urgent business reason (e.g., client escalation, force majeure) may result in the claim being reduced to the fare that would have applied at the required advance-booking window.

conditions.text: domestic tickets were booked at least 7 days ahead and international tickets at least 14 days ahead, or a documented urgent business reason exists

clauses.verbatim_text: 3.3. **Lowest logical fare.** Employees must select the lowest-cost itinerary within a 2-hour window of the required departure/arrival time, on a reasonably direct routing (at most one reasonable connection for domestic, at most two for international).

conditions.text: Selected itinerary must be the lowest‑cost option within a 2‑hour window of the required departure/arrival time and may include at most one reasonable connection for domestic flights or at most two for international flights

clauses.verbatim_text:
3.4. **Class of travel — domestic flights**

| Grade | Class |
|---|---|
| L1 | Economy |
| L2 | Economy |
| L3 | Economy (Economy Plus / extra-legroom permitted for flights over 3 hours) |
| L4 | Economy Plus / Premium Economy |
| L5 | Business permitted for flights over 3 hours; otherwise Economy Plus |
| L6 | Business, any duration |

conditions.text: Allowed travel class is determined by employee grade as per the domestic flight class table

clauses.verbatim_text:
3.5. **Class of travel — international flights**

| Grade | Under 6 hours | 6 hours and over |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | Economy | Economy |
| L2 | Economy | Economy |
| L3 | Economy | Premium Economy |
| L4 | Premium Economy | Business (Department Head pre-approval required) |
| L5 | Business | Business |
| L6 | Business | Business (First Class at the Executive's discretion, logged as a policy exception per §23.4) |

conditions.text: Allowed travel class for international flights is determined by employee grade (and flight duration) as per the international flight class table

clauses.verbatim_text: 3.6. **Baggage and seat fees.** One checked bag within the airline's standard allowance is reimbursable for any flight. Extra baggage requires a stated business reason (e.g., client deliverables, demo hardware). Seat-selection fees are reimbursable only for L4 and above on flights over 3 hours; otherwise not reimbursable.

conditions.text: One checked bag within the airline's standard allowance is reimbursable; extra baggage requires a documented business reason
Seat‑selection fees are reimbursable only for grades L4 and above on flights longer than 3 hours

clauses.verbatim_text: 3.7. **Cancellation and change fees.** Reimbursable when the change is driven by a genuine business reason (client reschedule, itinerary change directed by a manager, illness, force majeure) with Reporting Manager approval. Not reimbursable when the change is for personal convenience.

conditions.text: Cancellation or change fees are reimbursable when driven by a genuine business reason and approved by the Reporting Manager
Cancellation or change fees are not reimbursable when the change is for personal convenience

clauses.verbatim_text:
4.1. **Class of travel by grade**

| Grade | Rail | Intercity bus |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | AC 3-Tier / AC Chair Car | AC Seater |
| L2 | AC 3-Tier / AC Chair Car | AC Seater |
| L3 | AC 2-Tier / Executive Chair Car | AC Sleeper |
| L4 | AC 2-Tier / Executive Chair Car | AC Sleeper |
| L5 | AC First Class | AC Sleeper |
| L6 | AC First Class / Executive | AC Sleeper |

conditions.text: Travel class must be one of the allowed classes for the employee's grade

clauses.notes: Only applies to intercity travel tickets (rail or bus) and defines allowed classes per grade.

clauses.verbatim_text: 4.2. Rail or bus should be preferred over air travel for routes under 400 km or under 5 hours' journey time where a reasonable service exists, unless the business schedule requires air travel.
clauses.notes: Guidance only; not checked.

clauses.verbatim_text:
5.1. **Ride-hailing and cabs — allowed vehicle tier by grade**

| Grade | Allowed tier |
|---|---|
| L1 – L3 | Economy / hatchback-sedan tier (e.g., "Go"/"Mini"-equivalent) |
| L4 – L5 | Sedan / Premium Sedan |
| L6 | Any tier, including premium |

conditions.text: Employee grade must be within the allowed vehicle tier for ride‑hailing/cab

clauses.notes: Tier restriction only; no monetary cap.

clauses.verbatim_text: 5.2. Premium tiers (SUV, luxury sedan) above an employee's allowed tier are not reimbursable unless no alternative is available — e.g., group travel with colleagues, heavy equipment/luggage, or no lower-tier vehicle available at the time — and the reason is noted on the claim.

conditions.text: Expense is for a premium tier vehicle above the employee’s allowed tier
No lower‑tier vehicle or alternative is available, or travel is with a group/heavy luggage, and the reason is noted on the claim

clauses.notes: Premium‑tier rides are blocked unless justified.

clauses.verbatim_text:
5.3. **Per-ride cap**

| City tier / zone | Cap per ride |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | ₹800 |
| Tier 2 | ₹500 |
| Tier 3 | ₹400 |
| International (Zone A) | $35 |
| International (Zone B) | $25 |

5.3.1. **Airport transfers.** A cab or ride-hailing trip to or from the airport is reimbursable as local transport under this clause, at the applicable per-ride cap; it is a separate expense from the flight itself (§3), which is booked and claimed under intercity travel.
clauses.notes: Airport transfers follow the per‑ride caps in clause 5.3.

clauses.verbatim_text: 5.3.2. **Late-night travel.** A cab home after 9:00 PM for safety reasons is reimbursable at the standard allowed tier for the employee's grade, regardless of whether the employee would normally use public transport, provided the late finish was for a genuine business reason (client call, release, event).

conditions.text: Ride occurs after 9:00 PM and the late finish is for a genuine business reason

clauses.notes: Allows standard tier even if employee would normally use public transport.

clauses.verbatim_text: 5.4. Auto-rickshaw, metro, and other public transport fares are reimbursable at actuals with a receipt or a digital payment record (e.g., metro card top-up receipt, UPI payment screenshot showing the vendor).
clauses.notes: Auto‑rickshaw, metro, etc. reimbursed at actuals with receipt.

clauses.verbatim_text: 5.5. Parking and toll charges incurred during business travel are reimbursable at actuals with a receipt.
clauses.notes: Parking and toll charges reimbursed at actuals with receipt.

clauses.verbatim_text: 5.6. **Daily commute excluded.** The employee's regular home-to-office and office-to-home commute is never reimbursable, regardless of grade, except for the late-night safety exception in §5.3.2.

conditions.text: Expense is the employee’s regular home‑to‑office or office‑to‑home commute
Late‑night safety exception applies as per clause 5.3.2

clauses.notes: Daily commute not reimbursable except for approved late‑night safety rides.

clauses.verbatim_text: 6.1. Employees who use their own two-wheeler or four-wheeler for business travel (client visits, inter-office travel) may claim mileage instead of actual fuel cost.

6.2. **Per-km rates**

| Vehicle | Rate |
|---|---|
| Two-wheeler | ₹4 / km |
| Four-wheeler | ₹9 / km |

6.3. **Monthly cap by grade**

| Grade | Monthly cap |
|---|---|
| L1 – L2 | ₹3,000 |
| L3 – L4 | ₹5,000 |
| L5 – L6 | ₹8,000 |

6.4. **Trip log required.** Every mileage claim must be supported by a trip log recording, for each trip: date, place visited, purpose, client (if applicable), and kilometres travelled. A conveyance form without a trip log will not be processed.

conditions.text: trip log must be attached

clauses.verbatim_text: 6.5. Mileage and fuel (§7) cannot both be claimed for the same trip — an employee claims one or the other, never both, for a given journey.

conditions.text: fuel claim for the same trip also submitted

clauses.verbatim_text: 7.1. Fuel expenses are reimbursable at actuals, with a fuel station receipt, only for: (a) a company-leased vehicle, or (b) an employee at L5 or above who is on the company car policy.

conditions.text: company-leased vehicle OR employee grade L5 or above on company car policy

clauses.verbatim_text: 7.2. Fuel receipts must show the station name, date, quantity, and amount. A card slip alone is not sufficient (§20.3).

conditions.text: receipt includes station name, date, quantity and amount

clauses.verbatim_text: 7.3. Fuel and mileage (§6) cannot both be claimed for the same trip.

conditions.text: both fuel and mileage are claimed for the same trip

clauses.verbatim_text: 8.3. **Staying with friends or family.** In lieu of a hotel, an employee may claim a flat allowance of ₹1,500/night (domestic) or $40/night (international), self-declared, no hotel receipt required.
8.4. **Non-reimbursable extras.** Minibar charges, alcohol, in-room movies/pay-per-view, and spa/salon services on a hotel folio are never reimbursable, even if the hotel stay itself is within cap.

conditions.text: the expense is a minibar charge, alcohol, in‑room movie/pay‑per‑view, or spa/salon service

clauses.verbatim_text: 8.5. **Laundry.** Reimbursable only on trips longer than 5 nights, capped at ₹300/day (domestic) or $15/day (international).

conditions.text: trip length is greater than 5 nights
the expense is laundry

clauses.verbatim_text: 8.6. **GST invoice required.** A hotel bill of ₹7,500 or more (domestic) must carry a GST invoice showing Konkan Digital's GSTIN; a card slip or folio summary without GST break-up is not accepted above this amount.

9.1. Employees may claim meals while travelling either as a fixed daily allowance (per diem, no receipts needed) **or** as actuals up to the same cap (receipts required) — the employee chooses per trip, not per meal, and may not mix both methods on the same day.

|---|---|

9.3. Alcohol is never reimbursable under travel meals (it is only ever reimbursable under client entertainment, §10.3, within that clause's cap).

conditions.text: expense is alcohol

10.1. Meals or events with clients or prospects are reimbursable when the business purpose, client company name, and number of attendees are recorded on the claim.

client company name recorded on the claim
number of attendees recorded on the claim

11.1. **Per-head cap:** ₹800 for a routine team lunch/dinner; ₹1,500 for a celebration (birthday, festival, project milestone).

conditions.text: Expense is for family members or dependents accompanying the employee

clauses.verbatim_text:
The following are never reimbursable, under any clause of this policy:
- Purchase or top-up of loyalty points, airline miles, or hotel-status upgrades paid in cash.

conditions.text: Expense is purchase or top‑up of loyalty points, airline miles, or hotel‑status upgrades paid in cash

clauses.verbatim_text:
The following are never reimbursable, under any clause of this policy:
- Personal software/media subscriptions (§13.2).

conditions.text: Expense is a personal software or media subscription

clauses.verbatim_text:
The following are never reimbursable, under any clause of this policy:
- Alcohol, except within the client entertainment cap (§10.3).

conditions.text: Expense is alcohol (outside the client entertainment cap)

clauses.verbatim_text:
The following are never reimbursable, under any clause of this policy:
- Entertainment unrelated to business (movies, personal outings, personal gym/club memberships).

conditions.text: Expense is entertainment unrelated to business (movies, personal outings, personal gym/club memberships)

clauses.verbatim_text:
The following are never reimbursable, under any clause of this policy:
- Any expense already reimbursed by a client or under any other Konkan Digital policy or benefit.

conditions.text: Expense has already been reimbursed by a client or under another Konkan Digital policy or benefit

clauses.verbatim_text: 20.1. An itemised original receipt is required for any single expense of ₹500 or more (domestic) or $10 or more (international).
20.2. Below that amount, self-declaration (a short note describing the expense) is acceptable, up to a cumulative ₹3,000 per employee per month across all self-declared expenses.

conditions.text: the expense is below the 500 receipt threshold (self-declaration is only for these)

clauses.verbatim_text: 20.3. A card payment slip or swipe confirmation alone, without an itemised bill, is not accepted as proof of an expense.

conditions.text: proof is only a card payment slip or swipe confirmation without an itemised bill

clauses.verbatim_text: 20.4. Digital receipts (emailed invoice, PDF, clear photo/scan) are accepted provided they legibly show the vendor name, amount, date, and — where applicable — GSTIN.

conditions.text: digital receipt legibly shows vendor name, amount, date, and where applicable GSTIN

clauses.verbatim_text: 21.1. Domestic expenses must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date.

conditions.text: the expense is submitted within 30 days of the expense date

clauses.notes: applies to submission date vs expense date

clauses.verbatim_text: 21.2. Expenses from an international trip must be submitted within 60 days of the employee's return.

conditions.text: the expense is submitted within 60 days of the employee's return from the international trip

clauses.notes: applies to international trip expense submission

clauses.verbatim_text: 21.3. Ordinarily one claim per trip, or one consolidated claim per month for recurring expenses (phone, mileage).
clauses.notes: recurring expenses (phone, mileage) may be consolidated monthly

clauses.verbatim_text: 21.4. Claims older than 90 days from the expense date are rejected outright; there is no exception process for a claim submitted this late.

conditions.text: the claim is more than 90 days after the expense date

clauses.notes: no exception process for late claims

clauses.verbatim_text: 22.1. For a card payment, the conversion rate actually applied by the card issuer (as shown on the card/bank statement) is used.
clauses.notes: Conversion rate for card payments is taken from the card issuer's statement.

clauses.verbatim_text: 22.2. Where no card statement is available (e.g., cash payment), the Reserve Bank of India reference rate for the transaction date is used.
clauses.notes: When no card statement is available, the RBI reference rate for the transaction date is used.

clauses.verbatim_text: 22.3. For a cash currency exchange, the rate on the money-changer's own receipt is used, provided the receipt is attached.
clauses.notes: For cash currency exchange, the rate on the money‑changer's receipt is used if the receipt is attached.

clauses.verbatim_text: 23.1. **Auto-approval.** A claim of ₹5,000 or less with no validation flags (all arithmetic checks pass, no policy-limit breach) is approved automatically.
23.2. **₹5,001 – ₹25,000:** Reporting Manager approval required.
23.3. **₹25,001 – ₹1,00,000:** Reporting Manager and Finance approval required.
23.4. **Above ₹1,00,000:** Reporting Manager, Finance, and Department Head approval required.

23.5. **Policy exceptions.** Any claim that breaches a specific clause of this policy (an over-cap hotel night, a higher class of air travel than the grade allows, etc.) requires a written justification from the employee and approval one level above what the claim amount alone would require under §23.2–23.4.
24.1. **Duplicate claims** — submitting the same receipt or bill more than once, in the same or a different claim — are prohibited and treated as a compliance violation.
clauses.notes: Informational here: duplicate detection is Stage 4.

clauses.verbatim_text: 24.2. **Claim splitting** — dividing a single expense into multiple smaller claims to stay under an approval or receipt threshold — is prohibited.
clauses.notes: Informational here: claim splitting is Stage 4.

clauses.verbatim_text: 24.3. **Altered receipts** — any receipt that has been edited, whited-out, or otherwise tampered with — are treated as fraud, not a processing error.
clauses.notes: Informational here: tamper detection is Stage 4.

clauses.verbatim_text: 24.4. **Double reimbursement** — claiming an expense that has already been reimbursed by a client, another employer, or under any other Konkan Digital benefit — is prohibited.
clauses.notes: Informational here: double reimbursement is Stage 4.

clauses.verbatim_text: 24.5. Finance conducts periodic random and risk-based audits of submitted claims. A confirmed violation of §24.1–24.4 may result in recovery of the amount paid, disciplinary action up to and including termination, and referral to law enforcement where fraud is indicated.
clauses.notes: Informational.
